items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: I had never been in Speedy's place in my life but I knew -- someone told me that the six spirits of rhythm would go in every day

ctx.x: Well, I think Miles is now. But I mean, I think at that time Miles drank beer. I don't think he even smoked cigarettes at this time. But this was after the war, when I came out, you know, maybe it had something to do with the War hysteria, worst area, of conditions during the war, I don't know. Because I was in the army so I wouldn't know what was happening out in that area, you know, outside in that area. But I know that when I started smoking pot [my] -- I tell you, I went to pad

and I heard the six spirits of rhythm. Now, this Pad -- I had never smoked any pot, but I was an admirer of the six spirits of rhythm, you know, the -- Leo Watson and all of them. So there was a pad across the street from where I lived, the guy's name was Speedy, and I had never been in Speedy's place in my life but I knew -- someone told me that the six spirits of rhythm would go in every day and play and they'd get high, so I wanted to hear them play.

And I went over there and they were smoking pot, and getting high and playing and they would really play, you know. So I said, well geez, it can't be too bad if they can play. Now here we go, okay. If they can play and perform like that, it can't be too bad. I didn't smoke any then, but later I did. So it was a ball, you know, I laughed a lot and all of this, and I smoked it during that -- another reason I smoked it during that time, because my mother was ill, she was very ill, and we financially were in pretty…
